requirements.heading: Alignment and Extension Technologies
requirements.text: In the future, if DMARC is extended to include the use of other authentication mechanisms, the extensions MUST allow for the assignment of a domain as an Authenticated Identifier so that alignment with the Author Domain can be validated.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Explained
requirements.text: Where this is the case, the module performing DMARC evaluation MUST concatenate these strings by joining together the objects in order and parsing the result as a single string.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Explained
requirements.text: However, it is RECOMMENDED that Domain Owners use both DKIM and SPF as underlying authentication mechanisms for DMARC.

requirements.heading: DMARC Reporting URIs
requirements.text: A report SHOULD be sent to each listed URI provided in the DMARC Policy Record.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: Only tags defined in that registry are to be processed; unknown tags MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: adkim: (plain-text; OPTIONAL; default is "r".) Indicates whether the Domain Owner (Section 3.2.7) or PSO (Section 3.2.16) requires strict or relaxed DKIM Identifier Alignment mode.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: aspf: (plain-text; OPTIONAL; default is "r".) Indicates whether the Domain Owner or PSO requires strict or relaxed SPF Identifier Alignment mode.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: fo: Failure reporting options (plain-text; OPTIONAL; default is "0").

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: This tag's content MUST be ignored if a "ruf" tag (below) is not also specified.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: np: Domain Owner Assessment Policy (Section 3.2.8) for non-existent subdomains of the given Organizational Domain (plain-text; OPTIONAL).

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: If the "np" tag is absent, the policy specified by the "sp" tag (if the "sp" tag is present) or the policy specified by the "p" tag (if the "sp" tag is not present) MUST be applied for non-existent subdomains.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: p: Domain Owner Assessment Policy (Section 3.2.8) (plain-text; RECOMMENDED for DMARC Policy Records).

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: psd: A flag indicating whether the domain is a PSD (plain-text; OPTIONAL; default is "u").

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: rua: Addresses to which aggregate feedback reports are to be sent (comma-separated plain-text list of DMARC Reporting URIs; OPTIONAL).

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: A Mail Receiver that sends aggregate feedback reports MUST implement support for a "mailto:" URI, i.e., the ability to send a DMARC report via electronic mail.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: If the tag is not provided, Mail Receivers MUST NOT generate aggregate feedback reports for the domain.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: URIs involving schemes not supported by Mail Receivers MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: ruf: Addresses to which message-specific failure information is to be reported (comma-separated plain-text list of DMARC URIs; OPTIONAL).

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: A Mail Receiver sending failure reports MUST implement support for a "mailto:" URI, i.e., the ability to send message-specific failure information via electronic mail.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: If the tag is not provided, Mail Receivers MUST NOT generate failure reports for the domain.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: sp: Domain Owner Assessment Policy for all subdomains of the given Organizational Domain (plain-text; OPTIONAL).

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: If both the "sp" tag is absent and the "np" tag is either absent or not applicable, the policy specified by the "p" tag MUST be applied for subdomains.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: t: DMARC policy test mode (plain-text; OPTIONAL; default is "n").

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: v: Version (plain-text; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: This tag MUST be the first tag in the list.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Record Format
requirements.text: If the tag is not the first in the list, the tag is absent, or the value is not "DMARC1", then the entire record MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: Formal Definition
requirements.text: A DMARC Policy Record MUST comply with the formal definition found in this section.

requirements.heading: Formal Definition
requirements.text: Unknown tags MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: Formal Definition
requirements.text: Syntax errors in the remainder of the record MUST be discarded in favor of default values (if any) or ignored outright.

requirements.heading: Formal Definition
requirements.text: Because unknown tags MUST be ignored, the addition of a new tag into the registered list of tags does not itself require a new version of DMARC to be generated (with a corresponding change to the "v" tag's value), but a change to any existing tags does require a new version of DMARC.

requirements.heading: Formal Definition
requirements.text: dmarc-uri = URI ; "URI" is imported from [RFC3986]; ; commas (ASCII 0x2C) and exclamation ; points (ASCII 0x21) MUST be ; encoded

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Discovery
requirements.text: * If a "rua" tag is present and contains at least one syntactically valid reporting URI, the Mail Receiver MUST act as if a record containing "p=none" was retrieved and continue processing.

requirements.heading: DMARC Policy Discovery
requirements.text: If the set produced by the DNS Tree Walk contains no DMARC Policy Record (i.e., any indication that there is no such record as opposed to a transient DNS error), Mail Receivers MUST NOT apply the DMARC mechanism to the message.

requirements.heading: Publish an SPF Record for an Aligned Domain
requirements.text: To configure SPF for DMARC, the Domain Owner MUST send mail that has an RFC5321.MailFrom domain that will produce an SPF-Authenticated Identifier (Section 4.4.2) that has Identifier Alignment (Section 4.4) with the Author Domain.

requirements.heading: Configure Sending System for DKIM Signing Using an Aligned
requirements.text: To configure DKIM for DMARC, the Domain Owner MUST send mail that has a DKIM Signing Domain (Section 3.2.3) that will produce a DKIM-Authenticated Identifier (Section 4.4.1) that has Identifier Alignment (Section 4.4) with the Author Domain.

requirements.heading: Remediate Unaligned or Unauthenticated Mail Streams
requirements.text: For such legitimate uses, these shortcomings MUST be addressed prior to any attempt by the Domain Owner to publish a Domain Owner Assessment Policy (Section 3.2.8) of Enforcement (Section 3.2.9) for the Author Domain.

requirements.heading: A Note on Large, Complex Organizations and Decentralized DNS
requirements.text: To avoid this circumstance, Domain Owners wishing to have a specific DMARC Policy Record applied to a given Author Domain (Section 3.2.2) longer than eight labels MUST publish a DMARC Policy Record at that domain's location in the DNS namespace, as such records are always queried by Mail Receivers that participate in DMARC before the Tree Walk begins.

requirements.heading: PSO Actions
requirements.text: In addition to the DMARC Domain Owner actions, if a PSO (Section 3.2.16) publishes a DMARC Policy Record, it MUST include the "psd" tag (see Section 4.7) with a value of "y" ("psd=y").

requirements.heading: Extract Author Domain
requirements.text: If the domain is a U-label, the domain MUST be converted to an A-label, as described in Section 2.3 of [RFC5890], for further processing.

requirements.heading: Extract Author Domain
requirements.text: In the case where more than one domain is retrieved, the Mail Receiver MAY choose to go forward with DMARC validation anyway.

requirements.heading: Determine If Authenticated Identifiers Exist
requirements.text: * For SPF, the preserved results MUST include "pass" or "fail".

requirements.heading: Determine If Authenticated Identifiers Exist
requirements.text: If the result is "fail", it SHOULD include information about the reasons for failure, if available.

requirements.heading: Determine If Authenticated Identifiers Exist
requirements.text: The results MUST further include the domain name used to complete the SPF check.

requirements.heading: Determine If Authenticated Identifiers Exist
requirements.text: * For DKIM signature validation checks, for each signature checked, the results MUST include "pass" or "fail".

requirements.heading: Determine If Authenticated Identifiers Exist
requirements.text: If the result is "fail", it SHOULD include information about the reasons for failure.

requirements.heading: Determine If Authenticated Identifiers Exist
requirements.text: The results MUST further include the value of the "d" and "s" tags from each checked DKIM signature.

requirements.heading: Store Results of DMARC Processing
requirements.text: If the Mail Receiver intends to send aggregate feedback reports and/ or failure reports, then results obtained from the application of the DMARC mechanism by the Mail Receiver MUST be preserved for eventual presentation back to the Domain Owner in the form of such reports.

requirements.heading: Send Aggregate Reports
requirements.text: To ensure maximum usefulness for DMARC across the email ecosystem, Mail Receivers SHOULD generate and send aggregate reports with a frequency of at least once every 24 hours.

requirements.heading: Optionally Send Failure Reports
requirements.text: Per-message failure reports can be useful sources of information for a Domain Owner, either for debugging deployments or in analyzing attacks, and so Mail Receivers MAY choose to send them.

requirements.heading: Policy Enforcement Considerations
requirements.text: Such authorization does not carry an explicit or implicit value assertion about that message or the Domain Owner, and Mail Receivers MAY choose to reject or quarantine a message even if it passes the DMARC validation check.

requirements.heading: Policy Enforcement Considerations
requirements.text: Mail Receivers MAY choose to accept email that fails the DMARC validation check even if the published Domain Owner Assessment Policy is "reject".

requirements.heading: Policy Enforcement Considerations
requirements.text: In particular, because of the considerations discussed in [RFC7960] and in Section 7.4 of this document, it is important that Mail Receivers SHOULD NOT reject messages solely because of a published policy of "reject" but that they apply other knowledge and analysis to avoid situations such as rejection of legitimate messages sent in ways that DMARC cannot describe, harm to the operation of mailing lists, and similar.

requirements.heading: Policy Enforcement Considerations
requirements.text: At a minimum, Mail Receivers SHOULD add the Authentication-Results header field (see [RFC8601]), and it is RECOMMENDED when delivering messages that fail the DMARC validation check.

requirements.heading: Policy Enforcement Considerations
requirements.text: When Mail Receivers deviate from a published Domain Owner Assessment Policy during message processing, they SHOULD make available the fact of and reason for the deviation to the Domain Owner via feedback reporting, specifically using the "PolicyOverride" feature of the aggregate report defined in [RFC9990].

requirements.heading: Policy Enforcement Considerations
requirements.text: To enable Domain Owners to receive DMARC feedback without impacting existing mail processing, discovered policies of "p=none" MUST NOT modify existing mail handling processes.

requirements.heading: Interoperability Considerations
requirements.text: It is therefore critical that domains that publish "p=reject" MUST NOT rely solely on SPF to secure a DMARC pass and MUST apply valid DKIM signatures to their messages.

requirements.heading: Interoperability Considerations
requirements.text: It is therefore critical that domains that host users who might post messages to mailing lists SHOULD NOT publish Domain Owner Assessment Policies of "p=reject".

requirements.heading: Interoperability Considerations
requirements.text: Any such domains wishing to publish "p=reject" SHOULD first take advantage of DMARC aggregate report data for their domain to determine the possible impact to their users, first by publishing "p=none" for at least a month, followed by publishing "p=quarantine" for an equally long period of time, and comparing the message disposition results.

requirements.heading: Interoperability Considerations
requirements.text: Domains that choose to publish "p=reject" SHOULD implement policies that their users not post to Internet mailing lists and/or inform their users that their participation in mailing lists may be hindered.

requirements.heading: Interoperability Considerations
requirements.text: It is therefore critical that Mail Receivers MUST NOT reject incoming messages solely on the basis of a "p=reject" policy by the sending domain.

requirements.heading: Interoperability Considerations
requirements.text: "Other knowledge and analysis" here might refer to observed sending patterns for properly authenticated mail using the sending domain, content filtering, etc. In the absence of other knowledge and analysis, Mail Receivers MUST treat such failing mail as if the policy were "p=quarantine" rather than "p=reject".

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST send mail so it produces an SPF-Authenticated Identifier that has Identifier Alignment with the Author Domain.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST send mail that has a DKIM Signing Domain that will produce a DKIM-Authenticated Identifier that has Identifier Alignment with the Author Domain.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST set up a mailbox to receive aggregate reports and collect and analyze those reports.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST publish a DMARC Policy Record for the Author Domain and the Organizational Domain, if it differs from the Author Domain.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST NOT rely solely on SPF for a DMARC pass if the DMARC policy for the Author Domain is "p=reject".

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST check for the existence of a DMARC Policy Record for the Author Domain of an inbound mail message to determine if the DMARC mechanism applies to that message.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST determine if Authenticated Identifiers exist for the message and preserve the results of those checks for future use in reporting if the DMARC mechanism applies to the message.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST conduct necessary Identifier Alignment checks if the DMARC mechanism applies for the message and Authenticated Identifiers exist.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST use the information from the checks for Authenticated Identifiers to determine if the DMARC validation result is "pass" or "fail" for the message.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST support the "mailto:" URI for sending requested reports.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * SHOULD send aggregate reports on at least a daily basis.

requirements.heading: Conformance Requirements for Full DMARC Participation
requirements.text: * MUST NOT reject messages solely on the basis of a "p=reject" policy for the Author Domain.

requirements.heading: Failure Report Considerations
requirements.text: DMARC Policy Records for multi-organizational PSDs MUST NOT include the "ruf" tag.

requirements.heading: Secure Protocols
requirements.text: Unencrypted mechanisms SHOULD be avoided.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: Again, not all Mail Receivers will honor this request, but those that do MUST implement additional checks to validate that the third party authorizes reception of failure reports on behalf of this domain.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: Because the address used in the "ruf" tag is outside the Organizational Domain in which this record is published, conforming Mail Receivers MUST implement additional checks as described in Section 3 of [RFC9990].

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: In particular, this document makes explicit that domains for general- purpose email SHOULD NOT deploy a DMARC policy of "p=reject".
